ev.q: Age-adjusted hazard rates of incident laboratory-confirmed COVID-19 cases in both states were compared among cohorts
A lifetable method was used to calculate hazard rates
Estimated hazard rate is laboratory-confirmed COVID-19-associated hospitalizations per 100,000 person-days
compared with hospitalization rates among unvaccinated persons without a previous COVID-19 diagnosis
Rates were age-adjusted to 2000 U.S. Census data using direct standardization.
Four cohorts of persons aged ≥18 years were assembled via linkages of records from electronic laboratory reporting databases
These relationships changed after the SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant became predominant

methods_quotes.q: A lifetable method was used to calculate hazard rates
Rates were age-adjusted to 2000 U.S. Census data using direct standardization.
Supplementary analyses stratified case rates by timing of previous diagnoses and primary series vaccine product.
Life tables estimated at 7-day intervals for cases and 14-day intervals for hospitalizations.
